What most people completely miss is the massive sleight of hand that happened with India's nuclear program. If you look at the chronology, it is actually mind-blowing.
For decades, thanks to Homi Bhabha and our brilliant researchers, India led the world in Thorium technology. We literally filed the most patents globally. Then came the 123 Nuclear Deal. Everyone celebrated it, expecting it to boost our capabilities.
But what happened next? The UPA government quietly choked the funding for our homegrown Thorium research. The excuse? "We are getting Uranium from the West now, so we don't need Thorium."
Because private companies in India aren't allowed to work in nuclear tech, our top scientists were forced to look abroad. If you look up the US-based startup that recently made a massive breakthrough in Thorium fuel, the lead scientist is the exact same Indian researcher whose funding was cut back home.
Now, look at the supply chain. Where are India’s largest Thorium reserves? The beaches of Kerala. But since the 2000s, there have been highly coordinated protests by local fishermen, heavily guided by the Church, to block any mining in the area.
Connect the dots: Who funds these organizations? The West. Who benefits the most if India’s Thorium stays buried in the sand and we remain dependent on imported Uranium? The West.
It is a masterclass in geopolitical sabotage, and the rest of the country is completely asleep to it.

The Motive: Sir CP believed in the economic viability of an independent Travancore, citing its significant mineral resources, such as thorium as well as now known vast wealth hidden in the chambers of Sri Padmanabhaswami temple 
Negotiations with Pakistan: Muhammad Ali Jinnah welcomed the proposal, and Travancore aimed to sign a treaty for a mutually advantageous relationship with Pakistan.
The Shift: Following a failed assassination attempt on his life in July 1947 and the threat of political upheaval initiated by the local Congress and Communists , Sir CP resigned
